titulo: Why Does Voice AI Still Struggle With Kenyans’ Speech?
resumo: When people read prepared text aloud, AI can transcribe Swahili with remarkably few errors, and Swahili speech recognition looks close to solved. A March 2026 preprint by a team including a Harvard University researcher reports a 3.24 percent word-error rate on recordings from Mozilla’s Common Voice collection of volunteer-recorded speech. But Kenyans rarely talk like Common Voice volunteers. They switch between Swahili and English mid-sentence, drop in Sheng slang that changes by neighborhood, speak with accents shaped by their first languages, and contend with public-transport noise on low-end handsets. Another 2026 preprint , which covers 20 African languages, argues that this kind of spontaneous, noisy, overlapping audio exposes a generalization gap that scaling laws built on the English language have not closed. Voice has become a main interface for many Kenyans, as WhatsApp voice notes and chatbot voice prompts gain popularity in a country that ranks first globally on AI usage. titulo: RAID storage is confusing as hell. Here’s how to make sense of all the numbers
resumo: What is a RAID array? RAID stands for “Redundant Array of Independent Disks” or “Redundant Array of Inexpensive Disks,” depending on who you talk to. Note that the word array is included in the acronym, so saying “RAID array,” as a lot of people do, is redundant. RAID was created to combine multiple drives into a single, higher-capacity and/or faster volumes. It also facilitates data redundancy, also known as fault tolerance or failover protection , so that the array and its data remain usable even when a drive fails. You’ll often hear about 1-disk or 2-disk redundancy, which refers to the number of drives that can fail while the array remains viable. Redundancy is great, but it’s important to understand that it offers no protection against malware, theft, or natural disaster — and it’s certainly no substitute for proper backup practices . But as stated, it does make sure you can still access your data in case of drive failure.
